history.period: Main complex built 1867; Chandraprabha shrine added 1895
history.summary: NON-HINDU: this is a Jain (Śvetāmbara) temple, NOT a Hindu temple — keep-or-drop decision needed for Mahesh's dataset. Built in 1867 by Jain businessman Ray Badridas Bahadur Mookim at Belgachia/Gouribari (Badridas Temple Street, Maniktala, North Kolkata); consecration (pratishtha) by Sri Kalyansurishwarji Maharaj. A complex of 4 shrines: main shrine to Shitalanatha (10th tirthankara), plus Chandraprabha (built 1895 by Ganeshlal Kapoorchand Jahar), Mahavira, and the Dadawadi shrine with footprints of famous Jain monks Acharya Jinadattasuri (1075-1154 CE) and Acharya Jinkushalsuri (b. c.1280). Renowned for mirror-inlaid pillars, stained glass, chandeliers, marble inlay floors, painted walls (Ganesh Muskare paintings), gardens, fountains and a stream; a ghee lamp is said to have burned continuously since 1867 (unverified). One of Kolkata's most important Jain pilgrimage sites.

name: Parshwanath Jain Temple
town_description: Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal, is a major metropolis on the Hooghly river — India's cultural capital, founded as a British East India Company trading post (Fort William, 1698), and home to a large Jain mercantile community.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU), roughly 15 km away.
travel.railway: Sealdah station or Kolkata (Chitpur) station, a few km away.
travel.road: Badridas Temple Street, Gouribari/Maniktala, North Kolkata; reachable by taxi or bus from central Kolkata.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Paryushana (August-September) is the major festival period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 6 AM-12 noon and 3 PM-7 PM daily (reports vary: some say 6-11 AM and 3-7 PM; verify).
